title: Small Fires on Expressways or Roads Caused by Cigarette Butts
what_it_is: Small Fires on Expressways or Roads Caused by Cigarette Butts

sections.label: Vegetation fires and cigarette butts
sections.summary: SCDF attended about 350 vegetation fires annually between 2014 and 2017, mostly caused by cigarette butts, and offenders can be charged under the Environmental Public Health Act or Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2017, SCDF attended to about 350 such fires annually.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Most of these fires were caused by cigarette butts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: SCDF leads an interagency task force to deal with vegetation fires.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Among other measures, the National Environment Agency (NEA) regularly clears the roads of dry leaves, which are more susceptible to catching fire.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: But no amount of clearing will help, if some members of the public continue to illegally and irresponsibly discard cigarette butts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Such persons can be charged under the Environmental Public Health Act for littering at the least, and if we can prove the fact that the fires also cause serious damage, such persons can be charged under the Penal Code for fire-related offences.

sections.label: Difficulty proving cigarette butt fires
sections.summary: It is not easy to establish that a particular fire started from a particular discarded cigarette butt, so NEA takes a strict view of littering.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When you think of a vegetation fire, the fact is that it would not have started immediately, let us say, when a cigarette butt is discarded.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, hypothetically, even if someone happens to be at the right spot, at the right time, and manages to capture on camera or through video someone who had thrown a cigarette butt, it is not so easy to establish whether that particular fire started as a result of that particular littering incident.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are no easy ways to prevent, except to appeal to people's civic-mindedness, except to make it a habit of reminding people that whenever you discard a cigarette butt, whether it is in a housing estate or anywhere, that could lead to some other situation, such as a fire.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That is why NEA takes a very strict view of littering, especially when someone were to throw a cigarette butt.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am sure, as Members of Parliament, we have received appeals from our residents who tell us, "It was just that once" or "I wasn't thinking".

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But yet, NEA will have to take a strict view and really because, if it does result in a fire, it is not so easy to prove who did it.
